definitions.explanation: A surface or platform forming one level of a staircase.
A degree of proficiency or position in a hierarchy, especially in martial arts or traditional arts.
A section of text or a column in a newspaper.

examples.japanese: {階段|かいだん}を{三段|さんだん}{上|のぼ}る。
examples.english: To climb three steps on the stairs.

examples.japanese: {柔道|じゅうどう}で{三段|さんだん}を{取|と}った。
examples.english: I achieved third dan in judo.

examples.japanese: {新聞|しんぶん}の{一段|いちだん}に{記事|きじ}が{載|の}っていた。
examples.english: There was an article in one column of the newspaper.

notes:
COUNTER USE:
- {一段|いちだん}, {二段|にだん}, {三段|さんだん}...

MARTIAL ARTS RANKING:
- {初段|しょだん} (1st dan)
- {二段|にだん} (2nd dan)
- {三段|さんだん} (3rd dan)
- ... up to {十段|じゅうだん} (10th dan)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {階段|かいだん} (stairs, staircase)
- {段々|だんだん} (gradually, step by step)
- {段階|だんかい} (stage, phase)
- {段取り|だんどり} (arrangement, preparation)

NOTE: In martial arts, {段|だん} indicates high ranks (black belt levels), while {級|きゅう} indicates beginner ranks.
